iso29138.title: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 — Information technology — User interface accessibility — Part 1: User accessibility needs

V1.name: Visual information in other modalities
V1.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 5-1-2 concerns access to visual information through another sensory modality. Tasks can require non-visual access to visual content, controls, or cues, or preservation of auditory or tactile accessibility support for subsequent user interaction.
V1.iso_need_description: Visual information can be made available through another sensory modality.

V2.name: Adaptable visual presentation
V2.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 5-2-1 concerns individually suitable visual presentation. Its instances encompass information not conveyed by colour alone (5-2-1-c), contrast adaptation (5-2-1-d/e), and magnification (5-2-1-f). This need grounds tasks involving zoom, text enlargement, contrast, colour-independent cues, and other visual display adaptations.
V2.iso_need_description: Visual presentation characteristics can be adapted to individual perceptual needs.

V3.name: Text alternatives for non-text information
V3.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 6-2-4 concerns textual alternatives for non-text information. Relevant instances 6-2-4-a/b cover images and illustrations; tasks may involve accessible descriptions or text extracted from images, diagrams, maps, charts, scans, or visual verification challenges.
V3.iso_need_description: Non-text information can be understood using a textual alternative.

H1.name: Audio information in other modalities
H1.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 5-1-4 concerns access to speech and other audio information through non-auditory modalities. Captions or transcripts can satisfy user-facing access needs or be kept enabled for user takeover; the agent is not required to use those resources itself.
H1.iso_need_description: Audio information can be made available through other sensory modalities.

H2.name: Manageable textual presentation
H2.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 5-2-2 concerns readable, individually appropriate text presentation such as size, style, contrast, and layout. This cross-cutting need is instantiated here for caption or transcript presentation; caption language may additionally relate to ISO need 6-2-2.
H2.iso_need_description: Text presentation characteristics can be adapted to individual reading needs.

H3.name: Perceivable important alerts
H3.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 5-6 concerns appropriately perceivable important information and alerts. Instances 5-6-b/c cover visual or tactile attention cues, supporting non-auditory notifications when users cannot rely on sound.
H3.iso_need_description: Important information can attract attention through a suitable sensory modality.

H4.name: Adaptable auditory presentation
H4.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 5-2-5 concerns audio presentation suited to individual hearing abilities. Instances 5-2-5-a/d include volume adaptation and monaural access to multichannel information; tasks may involve mono audio, balance, and volume settings.
H4.iso_need_description: Audio presentation characteristics can be adapted to an individual listening need.

M1.name: Alternative input modalities
M1.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 7-1-1 concerns access to alternative input modalities. Instance 7-1-1-e addresses text entry, grounding tasks that preserve on-screen keyboard, dictation, or other accessible input options in place of conventional physical-keyboard entry.
M1.iso_need_description: People can use alternative sensory or interaction modalities to provide input.

M2.name: Non-simultaneous and self-paced action
M2.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 7-4-3 concerns operation without simultaneous input actions. Related need 7-4-4 addresses interaction at an individual pace. Keyboard timing and accidental-input accommodations (for example Sticky Keys and Filter Keys) are task realizations rather than separate ISO need definitions.
M2.iso_need_description: Input can be performed without requiring simultaneous actions.

M3.name: Alternative interaction methods
M3.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 7-3 concerns choosing usable interaction methods rather than relying on one conventional method. Tasks may preserve keyboard, speech, or alternative pointer operation; related need 7-4-2 addresses options for body use and handedness.
M3.iso_need_description: Functionality can be operated by an individually suitable interaction method.

M4.name: Reduced motor effort and demanding movements
M4.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 7-2-1 concerns manageable tactile or physical input, including limited force, sustained force, gripping, twisting, and movement. Related need 8-4 concerns physical exertion and 7-4-4 concerns self-paced interaction. Alternatives to dragging or precise repeated actions are benchmark-specific task realizations, not independent ISO instances.
M4.iso_need_description: Physical and tactile input demands can be adjusted to manageable force and movement.

C1.name: Reduced distraction
C1.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 5-4-2 concerns avoiding visual, auditory, or other distractions that interfere with attention. Tasks can preserve reduced interruptions, visual clutter, motion, or other attention-supporting settings.
C1.iso_need_description: Distracting stimuli that interfere with attention can be avoided or reduced.

C2.name: Reduced cognitive demands
C2.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 6-3-2 concerns reducing unnecessary cognitive demands in information presentation. Related need 6-2-1 concerns understandability. Tasks can provide simplified or structured explanations and summaries while retaining important information.
C2.iso_need_description: Information can be presented with a manageable cognitive burden.

C3.name: Memory and recall support
C3.definition: ISO/IEC 29138-1:2018 user need 6-3-4 concerns assistance with remembering and recalling information both during current activities and for future actions. Task realizations can include persistent notes, checklists, bookmarks, calendar entries, reminders, and timers.
C3.iso_need_description: People can receive support for remembering or recalling information.
